findings.finding: _unify()` replaces `sys.modules[__name__]` mid-exec when a loaded bare-name resolver already exists. This is the subtlest part of the change: the discarded module object keeps executing, and importlib's post-exec parent-package attribute binding is what makes the swap propagate. Any loader that caches the module object from `create_module` (or a custom finder) can end up binding the old object to `lib.shipwright_paths` while `sys.modules` holds the new one — exactly the split-brain the change is meant to eliminate.
findings.suggestion: In addition to the subprocess identity tests, add one assertion that after import, `lib.shipwright_paths is sys.modules["shipwright_paths"] is sys.modules["_shipwright_shared_review_lib.shipwright_paths"]` and that the parent packages' attributes (`lib.shipwright_paths`, `_shipwright_shared_review_lib.shipwright_paths`) point to the same object — attribute binding is the failure mode sys.modules checks won't catch.

findings.finding: When the bare name is absent, this module registers itself under `shipwright_paths` during its own exec. If any code triggered transitively by the module body (or by a later re-import race) does `import shipwright_paths` mid-exec, it receives the partially-initialized module. Also unhandled: the bare-name module present but partially loaded (circular import) — the plan checks `has SPECS`, which covers it, but only if `SPECS` is defined before any import that could recurse.
findings.suggestion: Ensure `SPECS` is assigned at the very top of the module body and document the invariant; add one test where `shipwright_paths` is imported first, then `lib.shipwright_paths` (order is claimed covered, just confirm it includes this direction).

findings.finding: Registering `shipwright_paths` when absent means previously-failing bare imports now silently succeed. A plugin with a typo'd or stale `import shipwright_paths` that today fails loudly will start working — masking an intended removal.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable (it's the point of the change), but note it in the brief so R1e's hook-matrix test doesn't get surprised.

findings.finding: AC5's subprocess hide test: `sys.modules["shipwright_paths"] = None` makes `import shipwright_paths` raise `ImportError`, exercising the fallback — but it does not exercise the case where the import succeeds and returns a module whose `rel` raises or returns `None` (a half-unified alias). If `_unify` misfires, hooks could take `rel()` results of the wrong module.
findings.suggestion: Add one variant test asserting that after any alias-order load, `_sp.rel("...")` returns the same value regardless of which alias the hook imported under.

findings.finding: The AST basename-discipline rule (AC6 static half) plus the fallback-literal AST scan are two bespoke static analyzers for a no-behaviour-change PR. Sound, but the "if more than ~8 hits, allowlist and defer swaps to R1b" escape hatch means the rule could land with known-failing hits — which will rot.
findings.suggestion: If the deferral triggers, land the rule in a reporting mode (or as a skipped test with a tracked count) rather than an allowlist inside a passing test, so R1b can tighten it without editing the rule.

findings.finding: new_rel`/`known_rels` are defined here but only wired in R1b/R1c; the spec explicitly says no production caller. Fine, but the ≤300-line cap on the resolver plus new helpers plus alias logic plus `SPECS` growth in R1b may force a move later.
findings.suggestion: Consider putting the alias-unification in a tiny separate helper module imported at the end of `shipwright_paths` — keeps the resolver clean and makes the swap logic independently testable.

findings.finding: None of substance. `classify` never executes or parses paths from stubs (`moved_to` text-only per 14.2), the recogniser is stdlib-only, and no new inputs reach production until R1c. Regex is anchored, first-line-only, byte-capped — good.

findings.finding: AC5 requires that every shared hook with a resolver fallback "imports cleanly with the resolver hidden and takes the fallback". The diff statically scans all fallback sites (`PAIRS`, ≥11 asserted) but only runs 4 hooks under `sys.modules["shipwright_paths"] = None` (`session_start_using_shipwright`, `required_checks_state`, `check_file_size`, `suggest_iterate`). The scan's own "must" list names `track_tool_calls.py` and `check_required_checks_hook.py` — shared hooks with literal fallbacks (BRIEF 12.7a) — plus `master_stop_check.py`, none of which is ever imported with the resolver hidden. A transitive unguarded `lib.` import in any of those hooks (exactly the dead-fallback shape discovered in `check_file_size`) would pass this test file undetected.
findings.suggestion: Parametrize the hidden-resolver import test over every distinct file the scan finds (at minimum the three named hooks), asserting `_sp is None` and the fallback literal is used, mirroring the `check_file_size` xfail pattern for any that fail for pre-existing reasons.

findings.finding: The scan asserts the exact AST shape of every `_sp is None` ternary at collection time. A hook that writes the fallback any other way (e.g. `"x.json" if _sp is None else _sp.rel(...) + ""`, or `_sp.rel(k) if _sp is not None else "x.json"`) raises `AttributeError`/`AssertionError` during collection — which is loud, so it's not a silent miss, but it means the "fallbacks written another way" fix promised in the architecture review is only partly delivered (the `except ImportError` branch is covered, the inverted/shaped ternary is not).
findings.suggestion: Either relax the assert to skip-and-record non-literal shapes (so a second test can fail on "unrecognized fallback shape" with a clear message), or accept the current loud-crash behavior explicitly in the module docstring.

findings.finding: BRIEF 14.1 specifies `^SHIPWRIGHT-POINTER/(\d+)$`; the implementation narrows this to 1–9 ASCII digits without leading zero, so a 10-digit version (`/1234567890`) or `/0`/`/01` returns `not_stub` where the spec's literal regex matches. The plan review signed off on `/0`, `/01`, and Unicode digits, but the 10-digit cap is a silent extra rule: a stub written by a future version numbering scheme would be misreported as `not_stub` (and thus read as config) rather than `too_new`.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep, but record the digit-count cap in the BRIEF 14.1 text (one sentence) so the fixture row `version_overlong` is spec-backed rather than implementation-invented; alternatively widen to `[0-9]{1,10}` and cap the `int()` conversion.

findings.finding: AC7's "byte-identical today" rests on `lib.config.CONFIG_FILES[skill]` returning exactly `shipwright_<skill>_config.json` for all six skills. The test pins the new output but nothing in the diff verifies equality with the OLD expression's output (`(_sp.json_path_or_none(skill + '_config', '') or Path(skill)).name`); if `json_path_or_none` returns `None` for a key whose file doesn't exist (its name suggests it may), the old line printed the bare skill name (`run`), and the new line prints the full filename — a behaviour change that this test would not catch. The AC record claims byte-identity was verified; the diff alone doesn't demonstrate it.
findings.suggestion: Add one assertion that `CONFIG_FILES[skill]` equals `json_path_or_none(skill + "_config", "").name` for every listed skill (or run the old expression in the test as the oracle), so the byte-identity claim is pinned by a test rather than by review prose.

findings.finding: This test mutates `sys.path` and imports `lib.shipwright_paths` inside the shared pytest process, after other test files (e.g. `test_shipwright_pointer.py`) have already inserted overlapping paths. It doesn't break anything today (unification is the point), but it means this test's outcome now depends on import order across the test session — exactly the fragility the file's own docstring says a shared process "cannot reset honestly". The other identity tests correctly use subprocesses; this one doesn't.
findings.suggestion: Move `test_known_locations` into a subprocess like its siblings, or relocate it to a file that doesn't claim fresh-interpreter isolation.

findings.finding: AC2 specifies `\d+`, but the recognizer accepts only one to nine ASCII digits and forbids leading zeros. `/01` therefore returns `not_stub` instead of `stub`, and `/1234567890` returns `not_stub` instead of `too_new`. An oversized signature with a long version also misses the `edited` verdict. The fixture matrix explicitly expects some of these conflicting outcomes.
findings.suggestion: Match the specified digit grammar and apply the size cap before converting the version. Use a length-safe comparison for arbitrarily long versions and update the fixtures to match AC2.

findings.finding: Concurrent imports under the bare and package names can leave two resolver objects. Python holds import locks per name, so the package import can reach `_unify()` after the bare module enters `sys.modules` but before it defines `SPECS`. The package import then returns its own object, and the bare import never reconciles it. The identity tests exercise sequential orders only.
findings.suggestion: Serialize initialization through a shared canonical loading path. Add a deterministic concurrent-import test that pauses the bare module before `SPECS` is assigned.

findings.finding: Any dotted name ending in `.shipwright_paths` is treated as a production alias. Loading the file as `probe.shipwright_paths` replaces the probe’s `sys.modules` entry with the live resolver, or makes the probe canonical if it loads first. AC1 requires probe isolation, and the test only checks an undotted probe name.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly recognize the supported aliases, including `_shipwright_shared_lib.shipwright_paths` if it remains part of the import contract. Test a dotted probe both before and after a production import.

findings.finding: AC5 requires every shared hook with a fallback to import cleanly and take that fallback. `check_file_size` still fails during its transitive import of `lib.bloat_baseline`, and the strict xfail accepts the failure. The `suggest_iterate` test also checks only that `_sp` is `None`, so it would pass if the hook read the wrong fallback file.
findings.suggestion: Make `check_file_size` importable with the resolver hidden and remove the xfail, or explicitly defer this part of AC5 in the acceptance criteria. Exercise `suggest_iterate` against a config fixture and compare paired `rel` fallbacks directly with `sp.rel(key)`.

findings.finding: The `event_seeder` check calls `seed._sp.name("events")` directly and never exercises the seeder. It would pass if the seeder switched to `rel()`, because the simulated layout leaves `events` at its legacy basename and both methods return the same string.
findings.suggestion: Give `rel("events")` a distinct directory-bearing value in the test and call the seeder’s basename-dependent behavior with a bare event filename.

findings.finding: The renderer’s SemVer validator accepts invalid versions such as `01.2.3`, `1.2.3-01`, and `1.2.3+build..5`, despite the documented `ValueError` contract.
findings.suggestion: Validate the core, prerelease, and build identifiers separately or use a compliant SemVer pattern. Add those inputs to the rejection tests.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The foundation is viable, but the recognizer diverges from AC2, module identity can split, and the fallback and basename tests leave explicit acceptance criteria unverified.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
